title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The notes concern a 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. X is a space with a stratification by closed subsets X_i indexed by a poset I, with X_j ⊂ X_i for j<i. The open strata are X_i^* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j. On the previous pages Grothendieck built 'link' data from chosen tubular neighbourhoods T_i and retractions: spaces Σ_i, Σ_ij and maps Σ_ij→Σ_i, Σ_ij→Σ_j, indexed by flags. He noted that this needs equisingularity and local-triviality hypotheses, and that the transition maps depend on the choices made.

What this page does. To remove that dependence on choices, Grothendieck switches to 'procespaces', i.e. pro-objects in spaces.

- **Pro-neighbourhoods of strata.** V_i (written V_i^*) is the pro-system of all tubular neighbourhoods of X_i^* in X: the germ of neighbourhoods, viewed as a pro-space.
- **(51).** He postulates that X_i^* → V_i^* is a homotopy equivalence of pro-spaces. This is a pro-version of 'a stratum is a neighbourhood deformation retract'.
- **(52), pairwise intersections.** For i<j he sets V_ij = V_i ∩ V_j. This gives a span V_i ←a_ij– V_ij –b_ij→ V_j, with V_i ≃ X_i (more precisely X_i^*).
  - V_ij is the part of the neighbourhood of the higher stratum X_j^* lying near the lower stratum X_i^*. It is a deleted-tubular-neighbourhood / homotopy-link type object. Under good hypotheses it should be homotopy equivalent to the link bundle Σ_ij of the previous page.
  - A margin question asks whether V_ij^* = V_i ∩ V_j^* gives a homotopy equivalence. This is exactly the comparison between the pro-intersection and the link Σ_ij, or the homotopy link.
- **Right-margin NB.** V_ij makes sense for any i≠j. If i and j are incomparable, the neighbourhoods can be chosen so that V_i ∩ V_j = ∅, and V_ii = V_i. This holds provided the open subsets of X are normal (X hereditarily normal, e.g. metrizable).
  - This is correct. For incomparable i, j, the closure X_i of X_i^* meets X_j only in strata of lower index, so X_i^* and X_j^* are 'separated' sets. In a hereditarily (completely) normal space, separated sets have disjoint open neighbourhoods.
- **(53).** X = lim→(V_i, V_ij; a_ij, b_ij): X is obtained by gluing the V_i along the V_ij. Level-wise this holds because the V_i form an open cover of X; pairwise intersections suffice, and incomparable pairs contribute nothing.
- **(54).** For a flag i_0<…<i_n he sets V_{i_0…i_n} = V_{i_0} ∩ … ∩ V_{i_n}. This is empty when the indices do not form a flag.
- **Next page.** These form an inductive system of pro-spaces indexed by the opposite of the poset of flags of I, i.e. the barycentric subdivision sd(I)^op. The next page then studies restriction to subspaces Z and to sub-index-sets J.

Purpose. The aim is to describe a stratified space, up to homotopy, by a canonical (choice-free, pro-) diagram over sd(I) whose vertices are strata and whose edges are link-type objects. X is recovered as its colimit. This is the 'déploiement' announced in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: Notation drifts between V_i and V_i^*. The homotopy equivalence written X_i ≃(h) V_i should read X_i^* ≃ V_i^* (the tubular neighbourhood is of the open stratum, as in (51)); X_i itself is not in general equivalent to V_i.

(53) is stated as a plain colimit of pro-spaces. Colimits of pro-objects are not computed level-wise in general, so it should be read level-wise for each choice of representatives. Since the V_i form an open cover with incomparable intersections empty, the level-wise statement is correct, and for numerable covers it is also a homotopy colimit.
The disjointness for incomparable i, j needs X hereditarily normal, as Grothendieck says. Without it, (53) would need to include incomparable pairs. This is a hypothesis, not an error.

(51) is not automatic: it requires the strata to be (pro-)neighbourhood deformation retracts, i.e. homotopically stratified / locally conelike conditions. Grothendieck flags this implicitly with the margin question.

ideas.what: Treat tubular neighbourhoods of strata as pro-spaces (germs of neighbourhoods), making the construction choice-free, with X_i^* → V_i^* a pro-homotopy equivalence
ideas.modern_name: pro-homotopy of neighbourhood germs; shape/strong-shape style neighbourhood systems
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pro-homotopy: Grothendieck (pro-objects, SGA4), Artin–Mazur, Edwards–Hastings (1976); for stratified spaces, Quinn's homotopy links (1988) play the analogous role
ideas.where_published: Pro-objects in SGA 4 Exp. I; the Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods of strata and 'déploiement' but not, to my knowledge, procespaces explicitly

ideas.what: Intersections V_ij = V_i ∩ V_j (i<j) as link-type objects, giving spans V_i ← V_ij → V_j, and higher intersections indexed by flags
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links / holinks of pairs of strata; the sd(P)-indexed link diagram (Douteau, Haine, Douteau–Waas)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); Woolf; Douteau and Haine (2018–2021) for the sd(P)-diagram model of stratified homotopy types
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 (dévissage of stratified structures into a system indexed by flags), in sketched form

ideas.what: Incomparable strata have disjoint neighbourhoods when X is hereditarily normal, since they are separated sets
ideas.modern_name: complete normality / separation of separated sets

ideas.what: X recovered as the colimit of the flag-indexed diagram of neighbourhoods: gluing the V_i along the V_ij
ideas.modern_name: descent along an open cover / homotopy colimit over sd(I)^op
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Čech/Segal); for stratified spaces cf. Lurie HA Appendix A, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the pro-intersection V_ij^* = V_i ∩ V_j^* is homotopy equivalent to the link object (Σ_ij of the previous page). He is thereby proposing a choice-free pro-space model of the homotopy link, to be compared with the geometric link built from chosen retractions. Under which hypotheses (Whitney, Thom–Mather, Quinn homotopically stratified) this pro-object is pro-equivalent to the holink is a natural question. It is not stated in this form in the stratified-homotopy literature, though Quinn/Hughes results essentially answer it in the homotopically stratified case.
missed.quote: Pour V_ij^* = V_i ∩ [V_j^*], a-t-on une équivalence d'homotopie ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A pro-neighbourhood model would give a canonical, functorial construction of the sd(P)-indexed link diagram used in current stratified homotopy theory (Douteau, Haine, Waas), without choosing control data.

missed.claim: This page together with the next one already describes a stratified space via an sd(I)^op-indexed diagram of (pro-)spaces built from neighbourhoods of strata and their intersections along flags. This is the shape of the modern 'diagrams over sd(P)' model of stratified homotopy types, which recent literature arrived at independently of these manuscripts.
missed.quote: on définit aussi, plus généralement, les V_{i0…in} = V_{i0} ∩ … ∩ V_{in} pour un drapeau i0<i1<…<in
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the flag-indexed (subdivision) model, beyond the brief sketch in the Esquisse; the pro-space formulation is a variant not found in that literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The flag-indexed déploiement is announced in the Esquisse, so the overall idea is known. Using pro-spaces of neighbourhood germs to make it canonical, and the explicit question comparing the pro-intersection with the link, anticipate later homotopy-link and sd(P)-diagram work. Still, it is a sketch with no proofs.
transcription_corrections: Margin note (52) reads roughly: 'Pour V_ij^* = V_i ∩ V_j^*, a-t-on une équivalence d'homotopie ?'; the '[?]' should be V_j^*.
Header '$\mathcal{V}_J^{[?]}$' is likely $\mathcal{V}_J^*$ (cf. X_J^* on the next page).
'Si $\mathcal{V}_{ij}$ $i<j$, on pose' is better read 'Si i, j, i<j, on pose'; the struck words before it are 'Pour un drapeau'.

Right margin: '(des voisins[?] si les ouverts de X sont normaux...)' should read '(des voisinages si les ouverts de X sont normaux, p.ex. X métrisable)'. The arrow attaches it to the claim V_i ∩ V_j = ∅ for incomparable i, j.
